hero.title: The Meat Grinder Needs More Meat
hero.subtitle: The billionaire panic vs. the biological scam.
hero.coldOpenHeadline: You know why the total fertility rate is in freefall worldwide and people simply refuse to have children?
paragraphs: Listen to politicians and tech billionaires whine on podcasts, and they will tell you civilisation is collapsing because people have become selfish. What they really mean is the meat grinder is running out of meat.
They do not care about procreation or the poetry of human life. They care about future taxpayers to fund old-age welfare deficits, and warm bodies to keep consumer demand humming.

anchors.label: The Ecological Deficit (Carrying Capacity)
anchors.detail: Humanity consumes resources at 1.73x Earth's biocapacity; demanding more people accelerates resource insolvency.

anchors.label: The 2050 Inundation Horizon
anchors.detail: Chronic coastal flooding and urban subsidence threaten Asia's primary low-lying economic hubs by 2050.

anchors.label: The Billionaire / State Contradiction
anchors.detail: Executives demand 'more babies to save civilisation' while deploying AI agents to erase entry-level careers.

hero.citation: Ref: Global Footprint Network (1.73 Earths Overshoot Index), Climate Central 2050 Coastal DEM & WEF Future of Jobs Report.

circles.label: Financial Sustainability
circles.sublabel: Upward mobility, cost of living, real savings

cards.headline: The Three Fundamental Circles
cards.body: Before a child can be brought into this world with a fair shot at a decent life, three fundamental circles have to intersect: family support, social policy, and financial sustainability.
cards.citation: Ref: UN DESA World Population Prospects, Replacement Level Fertility Threshold (2.1)

cards.headline: When the Circles Held Together
cards.body: In our grandparents' era, these circles held together. You had large extended families, neighbours who actually knew your name, and a baseline where one income could house and feed five kids. Upward mobility was the default expectation.
cards.citation: Ref: OECD Historical Household Income & Intergenerational Mobility Ledger (1970-2000)

cards.headline: The Middle Fell Through
cards.body: Somewhere in the early 2000s, at the peak of financialisation and hyper-efficiency, those circles drifted apart. The middle fell through. Today, governments toss baby-bonus cash into that black hole and wonder why the needle doesn't move. The biological function of continuing a species has somehow turned into an underpaid freelance gig.
cards.citation: Ref: KOSTAT (2024) & Singapore Dept of Statistics, Cash Subsidies vs. Urban TFR Floor

contradictions.title: The Grand Contradictions
contradictions.subtitle: Four structural paradoxes turning family planning into an impossible equation.

steps.title: The Automation Paradox
steps.subtitle: AI & Stolen Ladders
steps.copy: People breeding workers for a market that is aggressively automating them out of existence. Kids born today face a world where cognitive work is taken by models, entry-level career ladders are dismantled, and downward mobility into survival gig-work is the baseline. Raising a human to live without economic purpose is not a blessing; it is cruelty.
steps.metricLabel: ENTRY-LEVEL & COGNITIVE ROLES EXPOSED TO AI
steps.citation: Ref: Goldman Sachs Global Macro Research & WEF 'Future of Jobs Report' (2025)

steps.title: Sinking Cities (The 2050 Horizon)
steps.subtitle: 1.73 Earths & Rising Seas
steps.copy: By 2050, studies project major coastal metropolises, from Bangkok and Manila to southern Vietnam, will face chronic flooding and displacement from rising sea levels. We are currently consuming 1.73 Earths of biocapacity every year. The planet is literally choking on human extraction, yet leaders plead for more mouths to feed.
steps.citation: Ref: Global Footprint Network (1.73 Earths) & Climate Central 2050 Coastal Inundation Projections

steps.title: The "Paid Gig" Child
steps.subtitle: Financialised Shelter & Subsidies
steps.copy: In modern hyper-expensive cities, housing was transformed from shelter into an appreciating financial asset to flip. Now family planning has followed. Subsidies and paternal leave do not guarantee you keep your career trajectory, nor do they guarantee your child won't grow up trapped in a hyper-competitive rat race.
steps.metricLabel: HOUSING & CHILD COST VS. SUBSIDY TOKEN
steps.citation: Ref: Brookings Institution Lifetime Child Cost Analysis & Demographia Housing Affordability Index

steps.title: The Sandwich Meat
steps.subtitle: Sandwich Generation Trap
steps.copy: Today's adults are the sandwich filling: exhausted caregivers carrying aging parents past retirement on one shoulder, while being pressured to bear children on the other, with zero community support. The math does not work.
steps.metricLabel: WORKING ADULTS SQUEEZED BY DUAL CAREGIVING
steps.citation: Ref: Pew Research Center Intergenerational Care Study & OECD Old-Age Dependency Projections

propositions.title: Redefine the Family Unit
propositions.copy: The rigid state definition of a nuclear family, father, mother, and legal marriage, is completely outdated. If governments genuinely cared about raising well-adjusted kids, housing and childcare frameworks would open fully to cohabitation, single parents, and queer partnerships without the bureaucratic trap of traditional marriage.
propositions.citation: Ref: OECD Household Projections (2024-2040) & Family Policy Inclusivity Index

propositions.title: Normalise Dignity in Aging (Euthanasia)
propositions.copy: Nobody wants to admit that millions of elderly citizens are not spending their final years in picturesque peace. They are trapped in physical decay, feeling like indefinite financial burdens on their exhausted children. Open conversations about end-of-life autonomy and legalised euthanasia would restore dignity and relieve unbearable caregiver pressure on the generation in between.
propositions.metricLabel: FINAL-YEAR MEDICAL SHARE & PUBLIC AUTONOMY SUPPORT
propositions.citation: Ref: The Lancet Commission on the Value of Death (2022) & OECD End-of-Life Care Expenditure

propositions.title: Kill the "Growth at All Costs" Fetish
propositions.copy: You cannot prioritize perpetual GDP expansion and expect people to build healthy families. An economic model that demands infinite growth on a finite, overheated planet will always sacrifice human wellbeing for quarterly figures.
propositions.citation: Ref: Global Footprint Network Earth Overshoot Index & Hickel et al. (Nature, 2022)

conclusion.lead: People will have kids when they genuinely feel the future is brighter than the past.
conclusion.body: But when you look around at an unaffordable world, an unstable climate, and an automated job landscape run by billionaires who hoard the ladder, having less people is not a crisis. It is a biological correction. The planet is tired of us, and declining birth rates are simply society's immune response.
conclusion.punchline: Everything else is just noise from people who need more cogs in their machine.
conclusion.substackPrompt: Visual essays on power, generational economics, and street-level reality.
